intended_object: The chain map C_•(U; ℤ) ⊕ C_•(V; ℤ) → C_•(X; ℤ), (a, b) ↦ i_U(a) + i_V(b), from the Mayer–Vietoris short exact sequence of singular chains for open sets U, V ⊆ X. It is induced by the two inclusions. Inferred from the docstring, the name and its use in MayerVietoris.lean.
explanation:
The body is `biprod.desc (integralSingularChainMap U.inclusion') (integralSingularChainMap V.inclusion')`. Here `integralSingularChainMap f` is the map that Mathlib's singular chain complex functor with ℤ coefficients assigns to f. So on the biproduct the map sends (a, b) to i_U♯ a + i_V♯ b, which is exactly the sum map of the Mayer–Vietoris sequence.

The library pairs it with a difference map c ↦ (j_U♯ c, −j_V♯ c), where j_U and j_V include U ∩ V into U and V. It proves that the composite of the two maps is zero, and later relates this map to the small-simplices subcomplex. Both uses match the textbook sign conventions.

The library works with integral singular chains throughout, which is the standard setting for Mayer–Vietoris. The same map would make sense for any coefficient module. But it is a component of the library's integral Mayer–Vietoris construction, and Mathlib has no general version that this one duplicates. I see no discrepancy, including in degenerate cases: if U or V is empty, the chain complex on that side is zero.
